knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=Gene expression matrix where rows represent samples and columns represent genes ;; y=Survival data matrix or data frame containing "time" (survival/censoring time) and "status" (0/1 indicator, 1 = event, 0 = censored) columns ;; globalGraph=An igraph object representing the gene interaction network (e.g., KEGG pathway network) ;; nfolds=Number of folds for cross-validation in cvRLassoCox ;; s=Penalty parameter lambda value (e.g., "lambda.min", "lambda.1se", or numeric values) used for coefficient extraction and prediction
- alternatives: Standard Lasso-Cox model (via the glmnet package) which does not incorporate gene interaction network topology
- when_to_use: Appropriate for survival analysis and biomarker discovery using transcriptomics data when a relevant gene interaction network is available to guide feature selection
- pitfalls: Input graph objects created with older versions of igraph may trigger a warning to run igraph::upgrade_graph() ;; The survival data y must have columns named exactly "time" and "status" with "status" coded as 0/1 (where 1 is event/failure and 0 is censored)

workflows.name: rlasso_cox_survival_prediction
workflows.intent: Train a topologically weighted Lasso-Cox model with or without cross-validation to predict survival risk and identify prognostic gene biomarkers.
input: gene_expression.csv (matrix of gene expression profiles with samples as rows and genes as columns)
survival_data.csv (survival times and censoring status for each sample)
gene_network.rds (igraph object representing the gene interaction network)
workflows.stages: 1. Load gene expression, survival data, and the gene interaction network ;; 2. Split data into training and testing sets ;; 3. Train the RLasso-Cox model using network topology weights ;; 4. Predict survival risk on test data using the trained model ;; 5. Perform cross-validation to find the optimal lambda parameter ;; 6. Extract active prognostic features and their coefficients at the optimal lambda ;; 7. Predict survival risk on test data using the cross-validated model
workflows.code:
library("RLassoCox")
data(mRNA_matrix)
data(survData)
data(dGMMirGraph)
set.seed(20150122)
train.Idx <- sample(1:dim(mRNA_matrix)[1], floor(2/3*dim(mRNA_matrix)[1]))
test.Idx <- setdiff(1:dim(mRNA_matrix)[1], train.Idx)
x.train <- mRNA_matrix[train.Idx ,]
x.test <- mRNA_matrix[test.Idx ,]
y.train <- survData[train.Idx,]
y.test <- survData[test.Idx,]
mod <- RLassoCox(x=x.train, y=y.train, globalGraph=dGMMirGraph)
head(mod$PT)
plot(mod$glmnetRes)
print(mod$glmnetRes)
head(coef(mod$glmnetRes, s = 0.2))
lp <- predict(object = mod, newx = x.test, s = c(0.1, 0.2))
cv.mod <- cvRLassoCox(x=x.train, y=y.train, globalGraph=dGMMirGraph, nfolds = 5)
plot(cv.mod$glmnetRes, xlab = "log(lambda)")
cv.mod$glmnetRes$lambda.min
cv.mod$glmnetRes$lambda.1se
coef.min <- coef(cv.mod$glmnetRes, s = "lambda.min")
nonZeroIdx <- which(coef.min[,1] != 0)
features <- rownames(coef.min)[nonZeroIdx]
features.coef <- coef.min[nonZeroIdx]
names(features.coef) <- features
lp <- predict.cvRLassoCox(object = cv.mod, newx = x.test, s = "lambda.min")
